questions.question: What triggers the main conflict in Adam's story?
answers: The launch of a new Nintendo console
The news that Sony is ending disc production for new games starting 2028
A rise in television prices
The shutdown of Steam servers
questions.explanation: It is the headline about the end of new physical releases that triggers his reaction.

questions.question: Why does the phrase about a "revocable licence" affect Adam so strongly?
answers: Because he never bought digital games
Because it makes him realise the difference between access and actual ownership
Because he wants to trade licences
Because it applies only to films
questions.explanation: Adam links it to the risk of losing access to purchased content.

questions.question: What is the first concrete decision Adam makes after Sony's announcement?
answers: He sells all his games on disc
He cancels his PlayStation Plus subscription
He buys another console
He stops using the internet
questions.explanation: In the subscription section he goes into his account settings and cancels.

questions.question: What broader stake does Adam see after the statements by Ybarra and Mélenchon?
answers: A dispute over the colour of boxes
The question of consumer rights and the future of digital ownership
Only the French election campaign
A war between PC and mobile gaming
questions.explanation: He moves from fan anger to a dispute over digital ownership and culture.

questions.question: What does Adam's viral post express at the end?
answers: Anger at all online games
Readiness to give up a future console if the ownership model does not change
A request for free games from Sony
A plan to open a disc shop
questions.explanation: He writes that he will not buy the PS6 if Sony goes through with this plan.
